source_policy: Edit Mermaid in the owning chapter, then regenerate. No manual edits to derived files.

figures.title: From a User Request to the Next Action
figures.caption: The solid arrows show action choices. Dotted arrows show when new information or a decision calls for updating the brief. The figure omits the steps internal to execution. Readiness concerns the next action, and the brief records the basis for action without itself granting authorization. If the search yields no new lead and the gap still blocks the next action, pause that action. Independent authorized work can continue.

figures.title: Use a Question to Guide Each Step of Retrieval
figures.caption: The arrows show the proposed relationship between retrieval and selection for the current task. The dotted arrow returns to retrieval when there is a new lead. When a source is unavailable under the current authorization, record the gap or obtain authorization for broader access. Applicability in the figure concerns the current use. Check provenance and normative authority according to the type of source.

figures.title: Name the Recovery Target Before Deciding Whether to Proceed
figures.caption: This is a teaching diagram. An unknown write goes to readback first. Pause new effects that depend on the unknown state and allow permitted read-only investigation to continue. Restoring an entry point, restoring state, and starting another execution can coexist. Record each result separately. Compensation may lead to a named state from which work can continue. Reaching the historical state requires its own evidence.

figures.title: Can Earlier Evidence Support This Decision?
figures.caption: Solid arrows show how material enters a fitness-for-use decision. Dotted arrows return evaluable new results for another check. A valid test that observes a target failure supplies counterevidence and can support rejection or corrective work. A run that produces no evaluable result leaves an unknown. Retain earlier failures and acceptances alongside new results. A narrowly delegated gate or named role can issue a disposition. Reaching that step leaves the decision open until it is made. When no new leads remain, the budget is reached, or permission is insufficient, record the gap and stop dependent work or decisions. Independent work can continue.

figures.title: Continue With a Basis, Stop at the Boundary
figures.caption: Solid arrows show choices in the current pass. Dotted arrows reopen inspection with new material or refer a use to the authorized role. An ended review still leaves acceptance to the proper decision. A spent budget can leave issues open. Follow existing authorization for further actions and stop any currently unsafe action under the applicable rules.

figures.title: Information converges on a decision for the authorized role
figures.caption: Illustrative example. The upper arrows show how information converges, and the lower branches show options. Dashed lines mark the condition for reopening the decision and the limit of acceptance. Authority comes from existing rules or delegation. Sample results are hypothetical.

figures.title: Separate product input checks from QA applicability
figures.caption: Simplified mechanism from the case. The top group shows the recorded chain of erroneous propagation. The lower group lays out the two judgments in the repair. Their positions do not specify the actual call order. Product input includes required data and contracts for its source and consumption. The dashed line shows options when a decision needs the evidence.

figures.title: Keep the original question alongside candidate queries
figures.caption: Proposed mechanism. Solid edges show retrieval and decisions about use. The dashed edge returns to source readback after a targeted check finds a new source. Carry the original conditions through the final check. Merging candidates, targeted follow-up, and premise checks are proposed steps. Existing access permissions still apply to retrieval.

figures.title: A method comparison keeps positive and no-advantage results
figures.caption: Proposed mechanism based on the saved comparison. First check whether the evaluation answers the question. Then ask whether the candidate improved and satisfied its guardrails. Missing measurements leave the comparison open. The dashed branch indicates a correction that can occur in parallel. A valid review can find both drafts factually wrong, retain the no-advantage result, and correct the candidate. Improved objective performance with a guardrail failure stays outside adoption. The positive result has bounded scope and supplies no adoption, release, or overall efficiency decision.

figures.title: Check retained capabilities before retiring material
figures.caption: Figure 18-1 illustrates dependency-driven retirement. Check future capability against the required retention set. Evaluate deletion only for retirement candidates, and proceed only when the capability check and the checks for each candidate pass. Removing a reading entry, moving material into an accessible archive, and deleting its original are distinct actions. Partial reclamation leaves parent and failure-material holds in force until explicitly cleared. For historical explanation, check readability, provenance, and relevant relationships. A claim of recovery requires a corresponding recovery check.

figures.title: From a Metric Contract to a scoped conclusion
figures.caption: Figure 20-1 illustrates measurement disposition. If probe fitness is open, check start and end events, coverage, and the contract. Reassess when new evidence arrives. When evidence remains missing or the budget ends, retain the gap and suspend the conclusion. Correct a probe known to distort and check again with new observations. More samples from the old probe carry the same distortion. Report existing estimates alongside gaps after narrowing use. A passing point estimate settles only the part of the contract it addresses.

figures.title: How to Reduce Duplicate Records and Checks for the Same Task
figures.caption: Teaching comparison and proposed mechanism. The upper box illustrates repetition. The project history documents the actual changes, and the benefit has yet to be measured. The lower box shows conditional branches. The dashed line shows when work can re-enter after a stop. If a targeted check fails, keep the failure and return to the relevant problem. Risk and authority boundaries apply throughout. The result record leaves acceptance, adoption, and release to their respective decisions.

figures.title: Different Decisions in the Same Case
figures.caption: Historical relationships drawn from the [two scoped human decisions in SP122](../../Evidence/receipts/ER-20260827-001__CLM-C23-001.md). An undirected line shows coexistence, solid arrows show a named disposition relationship, and dashed arrows mark the limits of downstream authorization. The groups show decision objects. The candidate’s pending signoff remains part of history. The later closure accepted the D2 baseline containing v035 and the lifecycle-tag repair. Final Production Art and v4.94 Kickoff stayed outside its scope.

figures.title: FU05 route outcomes and cold restore
figures.caption: Figure 23-2 summarizes the recorded isolated machine paths. Other exception branches, wider balance, and adoption into the main project remain outside its scope. Experience and delivery scope have separate dispositions.
